newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin op possible "in next few days" - doctors.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin op possible "in next few days" - doctors.

text.p: Doctors treating President Boris Yeltsin met on Monday and said his heart surgery could take place in the next few days, a Kremlin spokesman reported.
Sergei Yastrzhembsky told Interfax news agency the doctors' council determined that Yeltsin was in "optimal" condition to allow the bypass operation to take place with maximum safety.

The doctors met at the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow where Yeltsin has been staying. They said Yeltsin's preparation for surgery had been successful and his current condition showed all organs and systems to be functioning at an optimal level.
"This makes it possible to undertake the operation with a high level of certainty and confidence," the spokesman quoted the doctors as saying.
"The operation itself can be carried out in the next few days."
Among the doctors taking part in the council was U.S. surgeon Michael DeBakey, who arrived in Moscow on Sunday.
